claims.head: Fresh legs vs. Tired ones
claims.body: The Hurricanes played last night and get no rest before this one. Teams in that spot usually get the worse of the chances, so we expect the Flyers to control more of the play than they usually do.
claims.call: The Flyers get a bigger share of the 5-on-5 chances than they usually do.

notes.text: Seth Jarvis is on the injured non-roster list and has not played this season. He is a top-six forward. Eric Robinson has taken his spot beside Sebastian Aho and Andrei Svechnikov.

faceoff.text: Jordan Staal is sent out to take power-play faceoffs, then changes. He has taken 71% of the team’s power-play draws but stays on for about 24 seconds at a time, against 63 for the regulars, and is most often replaced by Nikolaj Ehlers (8 of 10 changes).

PHI.head: Too close to call
PHI.body: Carolina has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately, but they are on the second night of a back-to-back, and Philadelphia has home-ice advantage. The Flyers can tip it if they keep dangerous shots away.

CAR.head: Anybody’s game
CAR.body: Carolina has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately, but they are on the second night of a back-to-back, and Philadelphia has home-ice advantage. For the Hurricanes, the difference could be keeping shots to a minimum.

story.head: A rematch of last spring’s second round
paras: The Hurricanes come in at 0-1-1, the Flyers at 0-1-1.
The Hurricanes shoot a lot, and the Flyers give up plenty. Expect plenty of hitting.

items.text: First meeting since the Hurricanes swept the Flyers in last spring’s second round, two of them in overtime.
Trevor Zegras has a point in five straight games against Carolina, with a goal in each of the last three.
The Hurricanes have been without Seth Jarvis all season.
Jordan Martinook is set to play his 800th NHL game.
